component.name: Where Did My Storage Go?
component.summary: See where your disk space went — as a colourful treemap
Sehen, wo der Speicherplatz hin ist — als bunte Treemap

description.p: Scans a folder or a whole filesystem and shows what is using the space as a colourful treemap: area is size, colour is file type. The big consumers jump out at you, a click zooms in, and anything you mark goes to the trash in one go — never deleted permanently.

Scannt einen Ordner oder ein ganzes Dateisystem und zeigt als bunte Treemap, was den Platz belegt: Fläche ist Größe, Farbe ist Dateityp. Die dicken Brocken fallen sofort auf, ein Klick zoomt hinein, und Vorgemerktes wandert in einem Rutsch in den Papierkorb — nie endgültig gelöscht.

ul.li: Shows at a glance which folders are eating your disk
Colours by file type, or by age to spot what you have forgotten
A sortable list view as well, when you want exact figures
Finds what can be cleared and totals up how much that frees
Moves what you mark to the trash, so nothing is gone for good
Refuses to touch system folders and other people's files

description.p: Sizes and times are written the way the chosen language writes them. Figures no longer show a stray extra separator.
Scanning the whole system no longer wanders into the desktop's internal mount points, so the figures match the disk and you stay in paths you recognise.
When system folders cannot be read, the app now says so and shows the one command that grants access, instead of leaving an empty view behind.
Packing a folder now shows how far it has got, and when it is done it says plainly what was created, how big it is and where it lies — with a button that takes you straight there.

Find things by name in both views — a single match blinks so you cannot miss it. The path bar now shows where you are in full, and you can click your way back up through it. Packing a folder that cannot be packed now says so straight away, and says why.
Where the trash cannot be used, the app now offers to delete the items permanently instead — as a separate, clearly marked choice.
Crash reports are now readable: they name the function and line instead of raw addresses, and the sections appear in the right order.
First Linux release. Native GTK3 port of the macOS and Windows app.
